newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Azomures splits its shares.
newsitem.headline: Romania Azomures splits its shares.

text.p: Romania's Azomures SA, a fertiliser maker listed on the Bucharest stock exchange, said on Wednesday it had lowered the nominal value of its shares following oversubscription in a mass selloff.

An official at the company based in the Transylvanian town of Tirgu Mures said a share split had been made after oversubscription, bringing the face value of a share to 1,000 lei from 25,000 previously.

State-run Azomures was part of a mass selloff which Romania launched in the autumn of 1995 offering Romanians stakes of up to 60 percent in around 4,000 state companies in exchange for privatisation coupons.
According to stock exchange data, Azomures has a share capital of 172 billion lei.

Azomures has yet to register in the exchange's registry its new mass privatisation shareholders and the split of its listed shares. Shares previously worth 25,000 lei will be divided into 25 shares of 1,000 lei each.
At the bourse's latest session last Thursday, Azomures -- the only stock to trade on the first tier thanks to its sound financial results -- closed 3,200 lei stronger at 27,200.
Brokers said they expected the new Azomures split shares to trade at around 1,500 lei when they enter the market. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
